⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • Como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game.
  • Cesc Fàbregas’s side revealed two things that rarely go together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

Como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

Cesc Fàbregas’s side revealed two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

In build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

In a recent development, close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

Como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

One detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

Recent findings suggest that for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

The decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

Sources indicate that what made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

According to recent reports, A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

When the build-up ran down the right, it showed in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

It has been revealed that in the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

Sources indicate that especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the upcoming ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

Recent findings suggest that como bridged the middle third exceptionally quickly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

Recent findings suggest that in this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

In a recent development, the connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

In the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

Recent findings suggest that the intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

Paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

According to recent reports, as the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

What carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

Industry observers note that united’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

Sources indicate that there were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

Sources indicate that mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

It has been revealed that on top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

Sources indicate that the second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened new spaces.

Recent findings suggest that in the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

Sources indicate that como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

The steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

According to recent reports, in the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

That isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

Once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

Sources indicate that the double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

Recent findings suggest that the last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

Recent findings suggest that when Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

Recent findings suggest that in the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

Up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

The pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

At half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

Sources indicate that the effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

It has been revealed that in the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

According to recent reports, accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

It has been revealed that deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

The crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

In a recent development, the numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

Tracking the ball for the first goal.

1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick promptly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

Sources indicate that what follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

In a recent development, 2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

The result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

In a recent development, 3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and demonstrates the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

Como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

It has been revealed that the common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

Como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

Industry observers note that the connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

For United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

According to recent reports, that leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What showed regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

Ce week-end avait lieu la suite de la phase de groupes pour la qualification à la CAN 2027 qui sera organisée par le Kenya, l'Ouganda et la Tanzanie.

Recent findings suggest that le Gabon de l'ancien Vert Denis Bouanga recevait le Lesotho. Les Panthères gabonaises l'ont emporté sur le score de 2 à 0. Deux buts inscrits par Denis Bouanga, qui aurait même pu faire un triplé. Alors que le score était encore de 0-0, il a manqué un penalty à la 64ème, juste avant de se rattraper et d'ouvrir la marque à la 65ème, pour enfin enfoncer le clou à la 79ème minute. C'était la 56ème sélection de Denis Bouanga, qui, avec ces deux buts, porte son total à 20.

Rappelons qu'il y a deux qualifiés dans chaque groupe. Après 3 matchs joués, dans le groupe A, le Maroc, avec 3 victoires est en tête, devant le Gabon (2 victoires, 1 défaite), le Niger (1 victoire, 2 défaites) et le Lesotho (3 défaites).

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents noted they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute mentioned the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF noted the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, remarked it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”.

E poi il popolo greco ha dimostrato di essere sempre al nostro fianco: sono la nostra forza e speriamo di renderli felici.

Dal punto di vista calcistico sto vivendo un ottimo momento alla Lazio. È una fase molto positiva per me, ma non ancora la migliore perché ho ancora tanto altro da dare.

Alors que bon nombre d'observateurs et de spectateurs ont considéré plutôt insipide la prestation de l'ASSE hier, en Coupe de France, contre le GFA Rumilly Vallières, alors que Ian Cathro lui-même concède qu'il ne va pas très longtemps penser à ce match, Cédric Rullier, le coach des Hauts-Savoyards considère, sur le site officiel du GFA, que, dans le contenu de cette rencontre, les Stéphanois ont montré des choses dont il va pouvoir s'inspirer :.

« Je tiens à remercier le FC Annecy dans son ensemble – dirigeants, staff, joueurs – qui nous a beaucoup aidé dans l’organisation, qui nous a laissé aussi l’intimité de son vestiaire. Peu de clubs l’auraient fait. Nous avions bien étudié l’ASSE et son projet de jeu vraiment très intéressant. Bravo au coach adverse d’ailleurs pour ça. Il y a des choses dont on peut s’inspirer. Sur le scénario du match, je dirais qu’on a été solides durant la première mi-temps avant de prendre le jeu à notre compte en début de seconde période, avec plusieurs occasions nettes, dont un but. D’habitude, on a un peu plus de réussite, et je pense que le match se joue là. Avec deux buts d’avance, l’issue aurait sûrement été différente. Bien sûr, il y a ce fait de jeu avec cette égalisation concédée à un de moins. Enfin, le fait d’avoir joué quatre jours avant s’est ressenti. Mais quoi qu’il arrive, je suis fier de la prestation des gars, face au meilleur club de Ligue 2. Maintenant, il faut basculer sur le championnat. Comme je l’ai toujours dit, la coupe, c’est éphémère. On a bien profité de ce bon moment et on va en tirer les enseignements. ».

Tech Report: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • Industry observers note that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Industry observers note that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Industry observers note that for the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

According to recent reports, “It highlights where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

Sources indicate that “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed significant character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

According to recent reports, A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a latest manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

Sources indicate that when Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Sources indicate that bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another upcoming signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

It has been revealed that justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Sources indicate that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

In a recent development, bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

In a recent development, that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Industry observers note that speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss noted: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

Industry observers note that A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. According to recent reports, it’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Industry observers note that what a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

With his current deal expiring in 2028, Scott has made an excellent start to this season, and scored a brilliant opener in Bournemouth’s 1-1 draw with Everton last weekend.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision-makers. Industry observers note that these meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernandez-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment team, “the one”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under upcoming head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

According to recent reports, despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Sources indicate that marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

In a recent development, at opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

According to recent reports, feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Il giudizio riguarda chi è rimasto a Roma durante la sosta; Agostinelli racconta anche di aver visto Frattesi sorridente.

In a recent development, la Lazio non ha staccato la spina durante la sosta: è questo l’aspetto che ha più colpito il protagonista dell’intervento riportato da Radiosei e che gli dà sicurezza per il futuro. A suo giudizio, i giocatori rimasti a Roma hanno mostrato di voler restare concentrati e di meritare spazio. Nel suo intervento ha parlato anche degli infortuni, di Frattesi e della sua conoscenza con Kurt Baldacchino.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

L’intervento si apre con una precisazione: «Premesso che la mia conoscenza con Kurt (Baldacchino, ndr) risale a tre anni fa.».

According to recent reports, lui è il presidente del ‘Lazio club Malta’ e appunto tre anni fa mi premiò quando allenavo l’altra squadra di Malta (il Gudja United Club). Quest’anno si divide tra la mia squadra, il Mġarr United, e le giovanili. Sapevo di questa cosa e pensavo si potesse risolvere. Quando siamo arrivati, io sono andato a casa mia a Roma e con la squadra e ci siamo rivisti direttamente a Formello, incontro Kurt, bravo ragazzo e tifosissimo della Lazio, e mi dice che era rimasto fuori. Eravamo però a ridosso della gara, quindi ho raggiunto la squadra. Speravo la situazione si potesse risolvere poi invece non è andata così e mi è molto dispiaciuto perché pensavo potesse essere un ‘giorno di festa’. Ad ogni modo è un ragazzo splendido, ognuno può esprimere le sue idee non gli darei ‘la croce addosso’. Probabilmente il fatto si poteva risolvere in maniera serena.

In a recent development, gli infortuni della Lazio? Avendo degli staff molto numerosi ci sono confronti continui. Oggi lo staff è molto importante. Frattesi l’ho visto sorridente. Per me un giocatore può fare mille cose atletiche ma lo giudico ‘guarito’ se fa una partita, anche solo di 15′ perché non sei frenato durante la partitella. Questo però non significa che non ci saranno rischi in gara.

Di questa Lazio l’aspetto che mi ha impressionato, e che mi dà sicurezza per il futuro, è che non hanno staccato la spina. Questo non è importante, di più. Significa che chi era a Roma durante la sosta ha voluto dimostrare di stare sul pezzo, di meritare spazio”.

Latest Update: Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Recent findings suggest that football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

According to recent reports, to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Industry observers note that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

According to recent reports, the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

It has been revealed that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

According to recent reports, the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

According to recent reports, the Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser noted it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players mentioned they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

Resté un grand supporter des Verts qui l'ont pourtant recalé plusieurs fois à l'adolescence au grand dam de Dominique Rocheteau, Lucas Da Cunha est "le grand gagnant de l'ère Zidane" comme l'a indiqué aujourd'hui Le Dauphiné Libéré.

L'AFP souligne les performances du natif de Roanne (Loire) en équipe de France, jugées "très satisfaisantes" par son sélectionneur. "L'ailier de formation a été placé en meneur de jeu par Cesc Fabregas en Serie A où il s'est révélé après quelques échecs en Ligue 1. Le patron des Bleus l'a encore fait reculer d'un cran en le plaçant dans un rôle de sentinelle où Da Cunha, qui découvrait le poste, a montré beaucoup de promesses et quelques lacunes, en défense notamment. Mais Zidane qui a procédé à une large revue d'effectif lors des deux rassemblements de l'automne, lui a accordé une confiance telle que le capitaine de Côme est le joueur de champ qui compte le plus de temps de jeu à égalité avec Michael Olise (386 minutes chacun).".

Industry observers note that dans sa dernière édition, la Pravda n'est pas en reste. "On dit d'un entraîneur qu'il couche toujours un nom en premier quand il compose son onze de départ. Concernant Zinédine Zidane chez les Bleus, on va finir par penser que ce nom est celui de Lucas Da Cunha, qui avait été le meilleur Français lors de la défaite en ltalie. Contre la Turquie, le meneur de jeu reculé a cherché à accélérer la circulation de balle des Bleus, qui manquait souvent de verticalité, tout en grattant plusieurs ballons au pressing ou grâce à ses anticipations (7 récupérations, record du match côté français). Depuis sa position basse, il est capable de renverser le jeu pour donner de l'air à l'équipe, mais aussi d'offrir de très bons ballons de but, comme il l'a fait deux fois pour Kylian Mbappé en dépassant son poste de sentinelle.".

Sources indicate that "Déjà un pilier de l'ère Zidane" dixit Le Parisien, le joueur de 25 ans savoure sur TF1. "Les compliments de Zidane sont géniaux, c’est exceptionnel. Il m’a donné beaucoup de responsabilités depuis que je suis arrivé. J’essaie d’appliquer tout ce qu’il me demande, que ce soit sur le proposal défensif ou offensif. Je sens que j'ai encore une grosse marge de progression, c'est ça qui est super intéressant pour moi. C’est sûr que l’ascension est folle. Il y a encore quelques années, j’étais ailier. Aujourd’hui, je suis milieu de terrain et je suis là avec les Bleus. Quand on commence le foot, quand on est jeune, c’est un rêve de pouvoir porter ce maillot. On rêve de ça. Et le jour où ça arrive, on n’y croit pas trop. J’adore, j’y prends goût. C’est une grande fierté d’être ici.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Sources indicate that referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst remarked. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

According to recent reports, “This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

In a recent development, van Bronckhorst mentioned he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

#26657. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

📖 Baca

VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?
  • Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.
  • Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

Recent findings suggest that the big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

According to recent reports, replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

In a recent development, on this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” mentioned Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi noted: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something vital.

Industry observers note that “If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with massive qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi noted: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

According to recent reports, after the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1.

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

According to recent reports, brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

It has been revealed that iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Enzo jeered by Coventry fans when taken off was predictable. Replaced by Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

In a recent development, forest are feeling aggrieved over that disallowed goal. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

In a recent development, major cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

That is a big chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca remarked, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more crucial to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

Recent findings suggest that “Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

According to recent reports, “I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just remarked he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very vital that he is with us.”.

Industry observers note that maresca remarked he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi aims to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

Contrairement à la Ligue 2 française, la Liga 2 en Espagne ne s’interrompt pas pendant la trêve internationale.

Le Cadix d’Aïmen Moueffek en a profité ce week-end pour ramener un bon nul d’Eibar (1-1). Hélas, malgré quelques absences dans le groupe, Aïmen est resté sur le banc.

Après le match le coach a dit toute sa satisfaction de ce point glané chez le 5e du championnat : « nous avons été bons tout au long du match. Durant les 90 minutes, nous avons fait preuve d'une grande rigueur. ».

Pas sûr du coup que Moueffek retrouve du temps de jeu le week-end prochain, lors duquel Cadix, 20e et relégable, jouera un match key sur la pelouse de l’équipe B de La Real Sociedad, 18e.

Pour Moueffek, prêté avec option d’achat et sous contrat à Sainté jusqu'en 2028, le bilan est pour l’instant mitigé. A date, il compte 1 but et 1 passe décisive et compte le 5e total des milieux de Cadix en nombre de minutes passées sur le terrain (3 titularisations après 14 journées).

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.
